title: The double-dual morphism restricts
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $A$ a finite commutative ring whose additive exponent is invertible in $k$, and $j:W\to Y$ an etale $k$-morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-ring module sheaves $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For $T=Y,W$ let $a_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism, put $\omega_T=a_T^\times A$ using the ambient compact-support right adjoint [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and put $D_TK=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,\omega_T)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $\delta_K:K\to D_TD_TK$ be the transpose of evaluation [lem-weil-duality-pairing], with the usual derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor].

There is a canonical natural isomorphism $\theta:j^*\omega_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_W$. Together with slice restriction of derived internal Hom it induces $\alpha_K:j^*D_YK\xrightarrow{\sim}D_W(j^*K)$. For every $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$,
$$\alpha_{D_YK}\circ j^*\delta_K=D_W(\alpha_K)\circ\delta_{j^*K}.$$
Thus the isomorphism $(D_W\alpha_K)^{-1}\circ\alpha_{D_YK}:j^*D_YD_YK\xrightarrow{\sim}D_WD_Wj^*K$ carries $j^*\delta_K$ to $\delta_{j^*K}$. In particular $\delta_K$ is an isomorphism if and only if its corresponding double-dual maps on a jointly surjective etale covering by separated finite-type $k$-schemes are isomorphisms.

The restriction calculation also holds on the small pro-etale sites with constant finite coefficients [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]: more generally, for any $\Omega_Y\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ set $\Omega_W=j^*\Omega_Y$, $D_T^\Omega=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\Omega_T)$ and let $\delta^\Omega$ be the evaluation transpose. Slice restriction gives the same displayed identity with $D^\Omega$ and $\delta^\Omega$ [lem-weil-duality-pairing, def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. Consequently it applies to a finite pro-etale realization with its specified compatible dualizing objects. This clause concerns ordinary constant-ring module categories; it does not assert an unconditional ambient pro-etale exceptional adjoint or identify them with condensed coefficient categories.

proof.text: The affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: the only ideals of a field are zero and the unit ideal. Its underlying space is a singleton, so it and every intersection of its affine opens are quasi-compact; the base of Nagata is therefore quasi-compact and quasi-separated. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $Y$ and $W$ are Noetherian. Nagata [thm-nagata-compactification] compactifies $a_Y$ and $a_W$; their proper compactification spaces are finite type over $k$ and hence Noetherian by the same finite-type lemma. Thus their ambient right adjoints exist by [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. The morphism $j$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation], since $a_W=a_Yj$ is separated. It is locally finite type because etale includes unramifiedness [def-weil-unramified-morphism], whose definition includes local finite type; it is quasi-compact because inverse images of affine opens of $Y$ are open subschemes of the Noetherian scheme $W$, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The compact-support assertion of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], applied to $f=a_Y$, $u=j$, and the constant input $A$ on $\operatorname{Spec}k$, now gives the natural isomorphism $\theta:j^*\omega_Y\cong\omega_W$. This use is only on ordinary etale categories and only over the finite ring $A$.

source.place: Proof, opening sentence: etale locality identifies the dualizing objects

proof.text: The node [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] applies to an arbitrary etale object $W\to Y$, despite its title containing the word open: its statement identifies $Y_{\mathrm{et}}/W$ with $W_{\mathrm{et}}$ and their covering families. Under this identification the inverse-image functor is restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]. This abelian-sheaf identification is $A$-linear: naturality for each multiplication-by-$a$, $a\in A$, gives linearity on constant sections; general sections of the constant ring are locally constant sections, so the sheaf axiom gives linearity everywhere. The restricted constant ring is $A_W$ by the same local description. Apply [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] to obtain exact module restriction $r=j^*$ and its exact left adjoint, slice extension by zero. Derived restriction is its termwise descent [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. No ordinary inverse image along a closed immersion is being substituted for a slice restriction.

source.place: Proof, restriction to the etale slice and exact extension by zero

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] on the small skeleton of $(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A_Y)$ with $L=K$, $M=\omega_Y$. It gives $rR\mathcal Hom_A(K,\omega_Y)\cong R\mathcal Hom_A(rK,r\omega_Y)$ for every, possibly unbounded, $K$. Postcomposition with $\theta$ gives $\alpha_K$. This node imposes no perfectness, finite-generation, or boundedness assumption. Its naturality supplies both the comparison for $D_YK$ and the contravariant map $D_W(\alpha_K)$ in the displayed equation.

source.place: Proof, restriction commutes with derived internal Hom

proof.text: Here is the compatibility with evaluation, including its derived models. Choose a K-flat flat-term representative $P$ of $K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and a K-injective representative $I$ of $\omega_Y$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Then $H=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I)$ represents $D_YK$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Restriction to the localization is a ringed-topos inverse image with unchanged ring sheaf; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] therefore makes $rP$ K-flat with flat terms. Also $rI$ is K-injective by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized]. On a test object over $W$, restriction of the Hom complex is literally $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(rP,rI)$: the same families of local module maps and the same differential $df=d_If-(-1)^{|f|}fd_P$ occur [def-pur-hom-complex]. Tensor restriction identifies pure tensors of sections and their sheafifications; the coverings on the slice over each test object are unchanged [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. It also commutes with direct-sum totalization, since sheaf direct sums are sheafifications of presheaf sums. Thus $r(H\otimes P)=(rH)\otimes(rP)$ with the same total differential [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. These are models for the derived tensors because $P,rP$ are K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Both evaluations on a homogeneous local tensor $h\otimes p$ are $h(p)$. After postcomposition with $rI\simeq r\omega_Y\xrightarrow{\theta}\omega_W$, this proves $\theta\circ r(\mathrm{ev}_K)=\mathrm{ev}_{rK}\circ(\alpha_K\otimes1)$ under the tensor comparison. The formula holds for all local tensors, which generate the tensor presheaf and its sheafification.

source.place: Proof, apply exact monoidal restriction to evaluation; K-flat and K-injective justification made explicit

proof.text: Take the transpose defining $\delta$ in [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. On the models of step 4 it is the map $P\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(H,I)$ sending a degree-$a$ section $p$ to the degree-$a$ map $h\mapsto(-1)^{ab}h(p)$ for $h$ of degree $b$; the sign is the tensor symmetry interchanging $p$ and $h$ [def-kun-derived-tensor]. The differential formula [def-pur-hom-complex] verifies this is a chain map: on degree-$b$ $h$, the coefficient of $d_Ih(p)$ cancels and the remaining term is $(-1)^{(a+1)b}h(d_Pp)$, which is $\delta(d_Pp)(h)$. Restriction preserves the degrees, the sign, and the application $h(p)$. Hence it preserves this transpose, not merely its source and target. Postcomposing the dualizing object by $\theta$ means that on the double dual the comparison is $(D_W\alpha_K)^{-1}\alpha_{D_YK}$, because $D_W$ is contravariant. Equivalently the two maps into $D_W(rD_YK)$ are exactly $\alpha_{D_YK}\,r\delta_K$ and $D_W(\alpha_K)\,\delta_{rK}$, and they have the same transpose under the tensor-Hom adjunction. More explicitly, let $\sigma:rK\otimes^L rD_YK\to rD_YK\otimes^L rK$ be tensor symmetry. Compatibility with evaluation from step 4, applied to $D_YK$, and the defining transpose of $\delta_K$ show that the transpose of $\alpha_{D_YK}\,r\delta_K$ is $\theta\,r(\mathrm{ev}_K)\,\sigma$. Naturality of transposition in the Hom argument shows that the transpose of $D_W(\alpha_K)\,\delta_{rK}$ is $\mathrm{ev}_{rK}(\alpha_K\otimes1)\sigma$. Step 4, now applied to $K$, equates these two maps. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves the displayed identity for arbitrary $\theta$ in the derived category, independently of any choice of chain representative for $\theta$. The signed formula above also shows directly that restriction preserves the symmetry used here.

source.place: Proof, transpose with tensor-Hom adjunction: explicit signed double-dual formula

proof.text: Let $(j_i:W_i\to Y)$ be the stated etale covering. Exactness of each $j_i^*$, supplied by step 2, makes $\mathcal H^n(j_i^*\varphi)=j_i^*\mathcal H^n(\varphi)$: kernels, images, and quotients in the defining cohomology complex are preserved. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-detects-iso] the underlying abelian-sheaf map $\mathcal H^n(\varphi)$ is an isomorphism precisely when all of its restrictions are. The inverse of an invertible $A$-linear map is $A$-linear (apply the map to $a\varphi^{-1}(x)$ and $\varphi^{-1}(ax)$), so forgetting the module action reflects isomorphisms. The criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], in every integer degree, proves the same equivalence for any derived module morphism $\varphi$. Apply it to $\delta_K$ and then use step 5. This proves the locality assertion without assuming $K$ bounded or using only the bounded-below criterion. For the empty covering, $Y$ is empty and the module category is zero, so the assertion remains valid.

source.place: Proof, an isomorphism is detected by a covering family

proof.text: An etale morphism is weakly etale by [det-pe-morphisms-etale-comparison]. The scheme $W$ is of finite type over $k$, hence a small scheme of the size convention, so $j:W\to Y$ is an object of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Hence [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies the small pro-etale site of $W$ with the localization $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}/W$, including its topology and constant coefficient rings.

source.place: Proof, last two sentences: the same slice calculation on the pro-etale realization

proof.text: On this localized ringed site, restriction and extension by zero are exact adjoint functors by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and derived internal Hom restricts by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Thus the derived restriction used here is the exact slice restriction of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction], with the constant-ring identification supplied by the localization statement.

source.place: Proof, restriction to the pro-etale slice and exact extension by zero

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose] to $\mathcal C=Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $\mathcal O=A_Y$, $U=W$, $K$ as given, and $\Omega=\Omega_Y$. With $\Omega_W=r\Omega_Y$, it gives $r(\operatorname{ev}^{\Omega_Y}_K)=\operatorname{ev}^{\Omega_W}_{rK}\circ(\eta\otimes1)$ under the tensor comparison.

source.place: Proof, last two sentences: specialize the arbitrary ringed-site calculation

proof.text: For $\Omega_W=r\Omega_Y$ let $\sigma:rK\otimes^{\mathbf L}rD_Y^\Omega K\to rD_Y^\Omega K\otimes^{\mathbf L}rK$ be tensor symmetry. By the transpose definition of $\delta^\Omega$ [lem-weil-duality-pairing] and the transposition/symmetry identities of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose], the transposes of $\alpha_{D_Y^\Omega K}\,r\delta_K^\Omega$ and $D_W^\Omega(\alpha_K)\,\delta_{rK}^\Omega$ are respectively $r(\operatorname{ev}^{\Omega_Y}_K)\sigma$ and $\operatorname{ev}^{\Omega_W}_{rK}(\alpha_K\otimes1)\sigma$, under the tensor comparison. Step 9 equates them; bijectivity of transposition gives the displayed identity. For a specified $\theta:r\Omega_Y\cong\Omega_W$, postcomposition sends both transposes to $\theta\,r(\operatorname{ev}^{\Omega_Y}_K)\sigma$, giving the compatible finite pro-etale realization clause.

source.place: Proof, last two sentences: transpose and compatible dualizing objects
